answer: A bond of 21% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in knoll, and karst reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 87 aliases, and each one needs its own funded inlet account. Scaling to 889 identities multiplies that fee by 702 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
